syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish syntax errors, runtime errors and logical errors in a Python program.
Explain how the interpreter detects and reports syntax (parsing) errors in shell and script mode.
Describe an exception as a Python object that represents an error raised during execution.
Identify the built-in exception raised by common erroneous statements.
Use the raise statement to throw a built-in exception with an optional message.
Use the assert statement to test an expression and predict when AssertionError is raised.

topics.title: Need for and process of exception handling

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why exception handling is needed and how it separates error code from main logic.
Describe throwing and catching an exception and the reverse search of the call stack.

topics.title: Catching exceptions: try, except and else

concepts.learning_objective: Write and trace a try...except block that handles a specific exception.
Trace programs with several except clauses, including a final except clause with no exception name.
Predict when the else clause of a try...except statement is executed.
State the position and purpose of the finally clause and when it is executed.
Trace how an unhandled exception is re-raised after the finally block executes.

topics.title: Introduction to Files and Types of Files

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what a file is and why data are stored permanently in files on secondary storage.
Distinguish between text files and binary files and identify examples of each.
Describe how lines in a text file are terminated by the End of Line (EOL) character.

topics.title: Opening and Closing a Text File

concepts.learning_objective: Use open() with the correct access mode and state the file offset position for each mode.
Identify the closed, mode and name attributes of a file object.
Explain why files are closed and how the with clause closes a file automatically.
Use write() to write a string to a text file and predict its return value.
Use writelines() to write a sequence of strings to a text file.
Use read() and read(n) to read all or part of a text file.
Use readline() to read a file line by line and recognise the end of file.
Use readlines() with split() and splitlines() to process the lines of a file.
Use tell() to find the current byte position of the file object.
Use seek() with an offset and a reference point to move the file object.

topics.title: Creating and Traversing a Text File

concepts.learning_objective: Predict how write and append modes treat a new or an existing file.
Trace a loop that traverses a text file and displays its contents.
Perform reading and writing on one file object opened in w+ mode.
Define pickling (serialization) and unpickling (de-serialization) of Python objects.
Use pickle.dump() and pickle.load() with binary files opened in the right mode.
Read all records from a binary file using load() in a loop handled by try...except EOFError.
Define a data structure and identify a stack as a linear data structure.
Explain the Last-In-First-Out principle and predict the order in which elements leave a stack.
Identify real-life and programming situations, such as undo/redo, browser history and string reversal, that use a stack.
Explain how a stack is used to check that parentheses in an expression are matched and properly nested.
Describe PUSH and POP and trace the contents of a stack after a sequence of these operations.
Distinguish overflow from underflow and identify the operation that causes each.
Explain why a Python list with append() and pop() can implement a stack without an explicit TOP.
Trace and reason about Python functions that push, pop, peek and display elements of a list-based stack.
Distinguish infix, prefix (Polish) and postfix (reverse Polish) notations and convert simple expressions between them.
Explain why prefix and postfix expressions need no parentheses to fix the order of evaluation.

topics.title: Conversion from infix to postfix notation

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the stack-based algorithm to convert an infix expression to postfix, tracing the stack and output string.
Use operator precedence and left-to-right order to decide when operators are popped during conversion.
Evaluate a postfix expression using a stack, tracing the stack after each symbol.
Apply popped operands in the correct order for non-commutative operators while evaluating postfix.

topics.title: Introduction to Queue and the FIFO principle

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how a queue follows the First-In-First-Out (FIFO) principle and contrast it with a stack.
Identify the FRONT (HEAD) and REAR (TAIL) ends of a queue and the operation performed at each.
Recognise real-life situations such as waiting lists and toll booths that follow a queue.
Explain why queues are used in computer science for web-server requests, OS job scheduling and print spooling.
Trace the effect of ENQUEUE and DEQUEUE operations on the contents of a queue.
Distinguish between the Overflow and Underflow exceptions in a queue.
Explain the role of PEEK, IS EMPTY and IS FULL in supporting enqueue and dequeue.
Implement a queue with a Python list using append() at the rear and pop(0) at the front.
Predict the output of Python queue functions such as dequeue, size and peek, including on an empty queue.

topics.title: Introduction to Deque and its operations

concepts.learning_objective: Describe a deque as a double-ended queue that can behave as a stack or a queue.
Identify situations such as browser history and undo options where a deque is useful.
Trace INSERTFRONT, INSERTREAR, DELETIONFRONT and DELETIONREAR operations on a deque.

topics.title: Implementation of Deque using Python and the palindrome check

concepts.learning_objective: Implement deque operations with Python list methods insert(0, x), append(), pop() and pop(0).
Apply the deque-based algorithm to decide whether a string is a palindrome.
Define sorting and identify the different orders in which numbers and strings can be arranged.
Explain why the overhead of sorting is worthwhile for searching data efficiently.
Describe how bubble sort compares and swaps adjacent elements over n-1 passes.
Trace the state of a list after given passes of bubble sort, including an early-stopping version.
Describe how selection sort selects the smallest unsorted element and swaps it into the sorted part.
Trace the partially sorted list produced by selection sort after given passes.
Describe how insertion sort inserts each unsorted element into its position in the sorted part.
Trace passes, shifts and comparisons of insertion sort on a given list.
Explain time complexity and how running time grows as the input size increases.
Estimate constant, linear or quadratic time complexity from the loop structure of an algorithm.
State and justify the quadratic time complexity of bubble, selection and insertion sort.
Explain what searching means and why it is an important technique in computer science.
Describe the key being searched and the possible results of a search.
Describe how linear (sequential) search compares each element with the key in order.
Determine the number of comparisons linear search makes in the minimum and maximum work cases.
Trace the Python linear search function and interpret the position it returns.
State that binary search works only on a list sorted in some order.
Calculate the middle index using floor division of first and last.
Trace binary search to find the iterations and the final values of first and last.

topics.title: Binary Search: Program, Applications and Comparison

concepts.learning_objective: Trace the Python binary search function, including its result when the key is absent.
Identify applications of binary search and modified binary search.
Compare the work done by linear and binary search for different keys.
Apply the remainder method to compute hash values and build a hash table.
Search a key in a hash table using the hash function with a single comparison.
Identify a collision and explain the need for collision resolution.
Explain a perfect hash function and evaluate whether a hash function avoids collisions.

topics.title: Introduction to Data and its Importance

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what data are and why raw data must be processed before decisions are made.
Describe how organisations use stored and analysed data for decision making.
Identify structured data organised in rows (observations) and columns (attributes) and compute from it.
Recognise unstructured data that has no fixed row and column format.
Explain metadata as data about data and identify metadata of files.
Describe how data are identified or gathered from appropriate sources and put into digital form.
Explain data storage, common storage devices and the limitations of file processing.
Describe the input, processing and output stages of the data processing cycle.
Classify the inputs, processing and outputs of real data-based tasks.
Calculate the mean and judge the effect of outliers on it.
Find the median of an odd or even number of sorted values.
Find the mode of numeric or non-numeric data.
Calculate the range as the maximum minus the minimum value.
Compute and interpret the standard deviation as a measure of spread.
Select a suitable statistical technique for a given data problem.
Identify the limitations of manual record keeping and the benefits of storing records in computer files.
Describe a file as a container of data and explain that application programs are needed to access file data.
Explain data redundancy and how it leads to data inconsistency in a file system.
Explain data isolation and data dependence as limitations of a file system.
Explain the difficulty of access and of controlled data sharing in a file system.
Define a DBMS, give examples and state what querying a database means.
Explain how related files are redesigned into tables of a database to remove redundancy.
State the costs and limitations of moving from a file system to a DBMS.
Distinguish a database schema from a database instance.
Explain data constraints and meta-data stored in the database catalog.
Identify queries and the insertion, deletion and update operations on a database.
Identify the relational data model among the types of data models.
Define relation, attribute, tuple and domain in the relational data model.
Find the degree and cardinality of a relation.

topics.title: Three Important Properties of a Relation

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the rules on attribute names, distinct tuples and the order of tuples and attributes.
Apply the rules on domains, atomic values and the use of NULL in a relation.
Identify candidate, primary and alternate keys of a relation.
Explain when a composite primary key is needed and identify one.
Explain how a foreign key relates two relations and restricts the values that can be stored.

topics.title: SQL, data types and constraints in MySQL

concepts.learning_objective: Describe SQL as a declarative, case-insensitive query language and the rules for writing its statements.
Choose suitable MySQL data types such as CHAR, VARCHAR, INT, FLOAT and DATE for attributes.
Identify the purpose of NOT NULL, UNIQUE, DEFAULT, PRIMARY KEY and FOREIGN KEY constraints.

topics.title: SQL for data definition: CREATE, DESCRIBE, ALTER and DROP

concepts.learning_objective: Create a database and a table and view the structure of a table with DESCRIBE.
Use ALTER TABLE to add or remove keys, attributes and constraints and to modify data types.
Explain the effect of DROP TABLE and DROP DATABASE.

topics.title: SQL for data manipulation: inserting records

concepts.learning_objective: Insert complete records with INSERT INTO ... VALUES, quoting text and date values correctly.
Insert values for only some attributes by naming the columns in the INSERT statement.
Explain why records of a referenced table must be inserted before the records that refer to them.

topics.title: SQL for data query: the SELECT statement

concepts.learning_objective: Retrieve selected columns and rows with SELECT, WHERE, aliases and DISTINCT.
Apply relational and logical operators, BETWEEN, IN and IS NULL in conditions.
Use LIKE with the % and _ wildcards and sort results with ORDER BY.
Modify values of one or more columns of existing records with UPDATE ... SET ... WHERE.
Remove selected records with DELETE and predict the effect of omitting the WHERE clause.
Predict the output of POWER, ROUND and MOD.
Predict the output of string functions such as MID, LEFT, RIGHT, INSTR, LENGTH and TRIM.
Use date functions such as NOW, DAY, MONTH, MONTHNAME, YEAR and DAYNAME.

topics.title: Aggregate functions and the GROUP BY clause

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish multiple row (aggregate) functions from single row functions.
Distinguish COUNT(*) from COUNT(column) when a column contains NULL values.
Group rows with GROUP BY and filter the groups with HAVING.

topics.title: Operations on relations and using two relations in a query

concepts.learning_objective: Apply UNION, INTERSECT and MINUS to two union-compatible relations.
Compute the degree and cardinality of the Cartesian product of two relations.
Combine related tuples of two tables with JOIN ... ON and NATURAL JOIN.

topics.title: Introduction to computer networks and evolution of networking

concepts.learning_objective: Define a computer network and state the advantages of sharing data and resources over it.
Explain what a node is and how data travels across a network as packets.
Describe the main milestones in the evolution of networking from ARPANET to Wi-Fi.

topics.title: Types of networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish a PAN and a LAN by range, media and data transfer rate.
Classify a given network as MAN or WAN from the geographical area it covers.

topics.title: Network devices: modem, Ethernet card, RJ45 and repeater

concepts.learning_objective: Explain modulation and demodulation performed by modems at the sender's and receiver's ends.
Describe the role of the Ethernet card (NIC) and the RJ45 connector in a wired network.
Explain why and where a repeater is needed to regenerate weakened signals.

topics.title: Network devices: hub, switch, router and gateway

concepts.learning_objective: Compare how a hub and a switch forward incoming data.
Explain how a router analyses, repackages and forwards data to other networks.
Describe the gateway as the entry and exit point of a network and its link with the firewall.
Describe mesh topology and calculate the number of links in a fully connected mesh.
Compare the direction of data flow, cost and reliability of ring and bus topologies.
Identify star and tree (hybrid) topologies and the effect of a failure of the central device.

topics.title: Identifying nodes: MAC address and IP address

concepts.learning_objective: State the structure of a MAC address and why it is a permanent hardware address.
Distinguish IPv4 and IPv6 addresses and explain why an IP address can change.

topics.title: Internet, World Wide Web and Domain Name System

concepts.learning_objective: Differentiate between the Internet and the World Wide Web.
Identify the roles of HTML, URL and HTTP and the parts of a URL.
Explain domain name resolution and the hierarchical arrangement of DNS servers.

topics.title: Concept and components of data communication

concepts.learning_objective: Explain data communication as the exchange of data between networked devices over a medium.
Identify the sender, receiver, message, medium and protocol in a communication.

topics.title: Measuring capacity: bandwidth and data transfer rate

concepts.learning_objective: Define bandwidth and calculate it from the frequency range of a signal.
Calculate data transfer rates and convert between bit-rate units.
Recognise one-way communication and its examples.
Explain two-way communication that happens in only one direction at a time.
Explain simultaneous two-way communication and how link capacity is shared.
Describe circuit switching with its dedicated path set up before communication.
Describe how packet switching breaks messages into independently routed packets.
Classify transmission media as guided (wired) or unguided (wireless).
Compare twisted pair, coaxial and optical fibre cables.
Compare radio waves, microwaves and infrared waves by frequency and properties.
Describe Bluetooth and the master-slave working of a piconet.
Explain how access points create a Wi-Fi (IEEE 802.11) wireless LAN.
Distinguish the features of 1G to 5G mobile network generations.
Explain why protocols are needed for flow control, access control and addressing.
Describe the working of HTTP and FTP on a client-server model.
Describe the roles of PPP, SMTP and TCP/IP in communication.

topics.title: Threats and prevention; viruses, worms, ransomware and Trojans

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish a virus from a worm by how each needs a host and how each replicates.
Explain how ransomware holds user data hostage and how a Trojan disguises itself as legitimate software.
Describe how spyware collects user information secretly and how adware earns revenue through advertisements.
Explain the threat of keyloggers and why an online virtual keyboard resists them better than an on-screen keyboard.

topics.title: Modes of malware distribution and combating malware

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the common routes by which malware reaches a computer.
Recognise signs of malware infection and choose suitable preventive measures.
Compare signature-based, sandbox, data mining, heuristic and real-time methods of malware identification.
Explain what email spam is and how spam filtering and user marking help.
Compare HTTP and HTTPS in terms of encryption and suitable uses.
Explain how a firewall filters traffic using rules and distinguish network and host-based firewalls.

topics.title: Cookies and threats due to cookies

concepts.learning_objective: Describe what a cookie is and the roles of session and authentication cookies.
Identify threats from supercookies, zombie cookies and third-party tracking cookies.
Explain the role of white hat (ethical) hackers in securing systems.
Classify hackers as white, black or grey hats (and hacktivists) based on their intent.
Explain DoS and DDoS attacks and why DDoS is harder to counter.
Identify intrusion attacks such as asymmetric routing, buffer overflow and traffic flooding.
Distinguish snooping from eavesdropping.
Identify the skills and practical exposure students gain through project based learning.
Describe how a project problem is analysed, broken into modules, solved and integrated, with data collected and reported in a set format.

topics.title: Approaches and steps for solving projects

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how a modular approach divides a project into modules whose outputs are integrated.
Sequence and describe the five steps of project based learning from identification to outcome.
Define teamwork and explain why complex tasks need collective effort.
Recognise the components of teamwork such as communicating, listening, sharing, respecting, helping and participating.

topics.title: Project 1: Automation of order processing in a restaurant

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the login, ordering and reporting requirements of the restaurant order processing project.
Explain why each bill needs a unique identification made from the date and the order number of the day.

topics.title: Projects 2 and 3: Puzzle and educational game

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the rules and exception handling needs of the grid-based bomb puzzle project.
Apply the rules of the 'Match the Sum' educational game to given situations.
